reason: Two narrow project skills guard the same dispatch module: which sessions automatic resume may restart, and where spend is counted so budgets cannot reset. Merged into one umbrella with a subsection each; the copied-home incident subfile is re-homed under references/.
A live demo run found that a closed-ticket agent replayed its script on the after-close turn, so sessions never ended; the dispatch skill is where agent session lifecycle rules live.
Peer notes added a new agent-to-agent path in dispatch; its storage, delivery and naming rules are non-obvious and the skill that governs dispatch should hold them.

Broadcast to every running session is a new dispatch fan-out with its own rules: system agent only with system=true, one kept line under session broadcasts that a name filter would pick up, and runners started before the change give no mark. The skill has a peer-notes section but nothing on broadcasts.
The per-session answer mode design and the fake-agent session-id trap were learned on this ticket and are dispatch-specific; the existing dispatch skill covers resume and budgets only.

Two test-harness traps hit while proving the dock change: insert on an existing session key, and a RUNNERS lookup that missed the worker's runner. Both are dispatch test mechanics a future session would otherwise re-debug.

Ticket #30 (3692a6ac) added a file-stamp skip to carry_spend, a nuance the spend section does not describe; a future edit could re-add an unconditional open or check only the main file and miss WAL writes.

Two dispatch facts from this episode: the fake agent's shared session id fails the second runner with a UNIQUE constraint on dispatch.sessions, and the permission answer must reach the agent before it is recorded (484 ms down to under 100 ms). Existing line on fake logs is extended, not contradicted.
